action_budget.detail: 16 executed ACTIONs, all canary baseline on the development pile. The stickiness probe spent 0: RESET is a command, not an action, and the scorecard counts only successful ACTIONs.

adversarial_review: The F-11 ledger text was reviewed by an independent adversarial pass (read-only, brief: find registration/ruling mismatches). It reproduced a fail-open bug in claim_set() and found four overclaims. All corrected; INC-006a records them. The ruling, the levels, the quarantine set and 21 -> 19 are unchanged.
artifacts_note: These sha256 values are over the working-copy bytes on a machine with core.autocrlf=true and no .gitattributes under arc-recon/. The committed blobs carry CRLF while appends made by client.py carry LF, so recon_ledger.jsonl currently has mixed line endings (790 CRLF, 194 LF) and these file-level hashes will NOT reproduce on a checkout with different eol settings. Content-level hashes are unaffected: piles.json's published sha256 is over a canonical re-serialisation, and the canary's hashes are over API response payloads. Pinning eol=lf for arc-recon/ the way engine-rig/.gitattributes does would fix it, but it normalises every file in the directory including the 2 MB append-only ledger -- left as an open item rather than done from a side branch during a merge round.
base_commit_note: the commit this branch forked from; master advanced during the ticket (another session), so `git rev-parse master` no longer names it
determinism: No stochastic step. The canary sequences are fixed and published in data/canary.json; its expectations were derived offline from precheck.json rather than sampled. The only non-reproducible inputs are live API responses, and every one of them is in data/recon_ledger.jsonl.
